headline: Generative and structured latent models infer, impute and simulate expression across space, age and kinetics
label: Generative Models For Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Preprints and papers pair generative simulators with spatial and kinetic structure to reconstruct, benchmark and interpret transcriptomic variation.
synthesis: The current items center on generative or latent-variable models that impose biological structure to recover unobserved expression states. For spatial transcriptomics, HoloGene lifts pre-registered slices to continuous 3D gene fields, SpaAxFormer models gene-resolved states across spatial neighbors for imputation, and multiCAsp uses a graph-Laplacian prior for spatial multi-omics. CroSP and CASTLE refine spatial context and domain detection with graph and contrastive learning. On the counterfactual side, scDeepSim enables controlled intervention on biological and technical factors for benchmarking, and scCody uses generative optimal transport to separate aging-aligned from divergent disease-associated remodeling. PhysInfer adds physics constraints to infer burst size and frequency from static scRNA-seq. The common advance is explicit structure, spatial, physical or population-dynamic, that makes inferred variation controllable. The set is only partly counterfactual; the spatial methods are mainly reconstruction and embedding.
